newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish minister fears privatisation glut in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Polish minister fears privatisation glut in 1997.

text.p: Poland's privatisation chief criticised his government colleagues on Tuesday for failing to align their plans for sales of large state firms in 1997 and said they risked glutting the market with offers.

Wieslaw Kaczmarek, deputy treasury minister in charge of privatisation, said plans for multi-million-dollar sell-offs by other ministers, coinciding with his own ministry's offers, could hamper chances for their success.

"There are four privatisation schemes of fundamental significance -- PLL LOT (the national airline), TPSA (telecommunications firm), banks and the PZU insurer -- originating in other ministries and there is a lack of coordination," Kaczmarek told financial journalists.

"If all of that is to be placed on the capital market I give in, because it is impossible unless we assume that most of our (privatisation) activities will be on foreign markets," he added at the briefing.
Kaczmarek said he was particularly concerned over the finance ministry's plans to privatise the country's leading commercial bank, Bank Handlowy SA, as early as in the first half of next year.
"Such initiatives, announced without consultation, are very dangerous for the market...because they may hurt privatisation prospects -- for example of Handlowy itself," he said.

He said the offer, combined with the treasury ministry's planned public offerings of the KGHM Polska Miedz SA copper giant and such large firms as Impexmetal SA metals trader and Polar SA white goods maker might create a supply glut the market could be unable to absorb.

Kaczmarek said the planned listing in the second quarter of 1997 of 15 National Investment Funds (NFIs), created under Poland's mass privatisation scheme, would also add to the supply of attractive bourse material.

The Finance Ministry has announced plans to float a minority stake in Handlowy next year and signalled it was willing to prepare a public offering of the country's top insurer Powszechny Zaklad Ubezpieczen (PZU) by the end of 1997.
The transportation ministry has announced plans to float up to 49 percent of the LOT air carrier by the end of next year.

The telecommunications ministry is due to present by the end of this month a plan for the TPSA former monopoly which might entail a first offer of the telecommunications company's shares as early as late next year.

Kaczmarek, who was privatisation minister until a government reorganisation last month, said other planned big-ticket sell-offs included a likely flotation of chemicals and fuels trader Ciech SA by the foreign trade ministry.
He said the need to coordinate privatisation efforts was particularily important ahead of several large-scale projects.
"So far we didn't have such problems because we had been working on much smaller projects. Now we are talking about sell-offs worth billions of dollars," Kaczmarek said.
He said that even though possible delays in some schemes might spread the supply more evenly, there was mounting pressure from managers to speed up work on privatisation deals.

"Delays can happen but now we have a situation that because of the imminent further opening of the Polish market to European Union competitition companies are keen to privatise and tap fresh funds as quickly as possible," Kaczmarek said.

The 1997 budget draft assumes privatisation revenues next year will rise to 3.5 billion zlotys ($1.2 billion) from an expected 3.2 billion this year. This figure does not include the possible sale of Bank Handlowy and of PZU. ($1=2.8140 Zloty)
